newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends mixed, spreading boosts March.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends mixed, spreading boosts March.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed mixed with nearby March higher on bull spreading with some citing arbitrage buying from the options pit as rationale for a portion of the late rally, traders said.
"There was a lot of March/May spreading and also they were buying Chicago March against Kansas City," a trader said.
FIMAT Futures did two million March/May and LIT America bought at least one million bushels of CBOT March and sold KCBT March, traders said.
Griffin Trading was a noted late spreader of the March/May, the traders said.
"March really took off when Griffin started bidding for the spread," a trader said.

A late rally in soybeans also buoyed nearby wheat contracts and the gains were posted despite keen competition for export business including confirmation a deal was struck between Australia and Japan, they said.
The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) Friday confirmed it sold at least 900,000 tonnes of wheat to Japan for delivery during 1997.
Wheat futures closed 4-3/4 cents per bushel higher to three lower, with March up 4-3/4 at $3.73.
"U.S. wheat export sales for the new crop (1997-98) are the lowest in 25 years so it doesn't look good," a trader said.
USDA Thursday, in its weekly export sales report, said total U.S. wheat export commitments so far this year were 23.537 million tonnes, well below the year-ago tally at 31.923 million tonnes.
Wheat Thursday rallied, led by gains in new crop months, on fund buying with Smith Barney accounting for at least five million bushels of the purchase, all of that in July.
Traders said the delivery notices posted Friday on the March at 2.24 million bushels were about as expected. Friday was first notice day for deliveries on the March contract.
Recent improved crop prospects in U.S. winter wheat growing areas due to precipitation in the past week also weighed on the July contract, traders said.
Traders said O'Connor and Co was a late buyer of three million bushels of July. On the day, selling of roughly three million July spilled over from the options pit, they said.
Options traders said Refco Inc was buying put spreads and selling calls which was adding pressure to the July futures contract.
Also on the day, SAK Futures sold 1.5 million July and E.D. and F. Man International sold 1.5 million July and bought 800,000 July, traders said.
Technicians early Friday said first support in the May was at $3.71-3/4 and second support was at $3.66-1/4. The session low for May was $3.68.
First resistance was at $3.77-1/4 and second resistance was at $3.82-3/4. The session high was $3.76-1/2.

The four and 20-day moving averages were giving off bullish signals early Friday, chartists said. The nine day relative strength index (RSI) for March closed at 58-1/2 percent. The market views an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 22,000 contracts, below the 31,410 traded Thursday.
In wheat options, Refco Inc bought 600 July $3.60 puts at 19-1/2 cents, sold 600 July $3.30 puts at seven cents and sold 600 July $3.90 calls at 10-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 8,000 contracts, above the 5,221 traded Thursday.
